data.title: AO3 is down and a 2 to 4 week wait begins
data.description:
Fanfiction readers and writers are facing a long wait. Archive of Our Own, better known as AO3, went offline today, and its operators say getting it back could take anywhere from two to four weeks.


The Organization for Transformative Works, the nonprofit that runs the site, first posted on its status page early Thursday that AO3 was down for maintenance. A few hours later, it said the work would take at least 12 hours. By the afternoon, the estimate had grown to about two weeks, with a month possible. The group said it hopes to bring the site back in a degraded state sooner, though it may have to take the site down again temporarily while repairs continue.


Why the outage matters

AO3 is one of the biggest homes for fan-created work on the internet. As of September, it hosted more than 18.4 million works across more than 82,900 fandoms. The timing is rough for many fans, since the outage covers Halloween, a major book release week for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses and the start of November, the month long tied to NaNoWriMo.

in case anyone needs a refresher: you can paste a fics URL into the wayback machine and read it as if you are on AO3. only catch is that newer fics are less likely to be archived. https://t.co/LjQnKZHQBI

— jay (@kendallhosseini) October 29, 2026

A rocky month for the site

Trouble had been building. On Oct. 14, the team acknowledged problems with uploading and viewing icons, which were fixed within a day. A rollout of translated email notifications began around Oct. 21, with Simplified Chinese first, and by Oct. 23 users reported issues with notifications, search and bookmarks. Those were also resolved within a day. The maintenance that triggered the current shutdown may be the same work that was postponed in August, though that has not been confirmed.

How fans can cope

Readers are not entirely cut off. Anyone with the link to a specific story or fandom page can try the Wayback Machine, which has saved many AO3 pages, though not all of them. From a saved fandom page, fans can click through to other stories that the archive has stored.

Writers who post directly to AO3 are being reminded to keep their own backups. The site is run by volunteers, and fans are being urged not to harass the people working to restore it.

since ao3 is going to be down for a while, i’ve added all of my completed loustat fics to a folder on g docs if anyone wants to read them! expect to find some minor errors/typos that i later fixed on ao3, but this is the best i can do for now lol 💖 https://t.co/ufIxfHSNSb

— Holly ✨ (@gruntsandpoetry) October 29, 2026

What comes next

The OTW has asked users to follow its status page and its X account for updates. For now, the site’s message simply says the archive is down for maintenance, and the fandom will be watching for any sign of an early return.

data.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with elite cybersecurity tools
data.description:
Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon today, Oct. 28, calling it its strongest AI model yet for coding, long running tasks and cybersecurity. Most people can’t use it yet. Google is giving first access this week to a small group of vetted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program, and developers, businesses and consumers will get it later with no firm date.


Carbon arrives just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google said on X that the new model ranks No. 1 on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Its score is 59.


What can Gemini 4 Carbon do?

Google built Carbon around the full cycle of cyber defense, which means finding a flaw, proving it is real and fixing it. The company reported scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploiting them and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching them, plus more than double Argon’s success rate at writing secure code in internal tests.

The gains reach beyond security. Carbon climbed 89 points to fourth place on WebDev Arena, a ranking of web development output. Google’s Chrome team found it more than 10 times better than another lab’s large model at producing high quality patches, and cloud security company Wiz reported it leading on web penetration testing. Google says its own engineers have used Carbon to run multiday projects, including tracking down and fixing bugs across large codebases.

Introducing Gemini 4 Carbon, our latest frontier model.

Carbon delivers improved performance across domains — ranking #1 on v5.0 of the @ArtificialAnlys Intelligence Index and sets a new state-of-the-art in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.

It’s rolling out starting this week to cyber defenders through our Fairwind Program, with expanded access coming soon 🧵

— Google (@Google) October 28, 2026

Why are cyber defenders getting Gemini 4 Carbon first?

Look at that second number again. A model that can exploit software flaws more than half the time is a tool that cuts both ways. The same skill that helps a defender confirm a weakness could help an attacker use one.

That is why access is gated. The Fairwind Program already has more than 650 partners, gives priority to governments, national cyber agencies, critical infrastructure operators and major technology platforms, and runs background checks on applicants. Google is also taking part in the U.S. government’s voluntary testing process for models before release.

There is another detail most coverage missed. Google measured those cyber benchmark scores without guardrails in place. Google DeepMind’s Koray Kavukcuoglu said in a blog post that wider access will come once the company gathers more feedback on those guardrails. The public version could behave differently from the one that set the records.

Is Gemini 4 Carbon more honest than older models?

Google says it is. According to the company, Carbon makes roughly half as many unsupported claims as Argon, writes caveats directly into its work instead of guessing and flags conflicting information before acting. Google also reports a 26% drop in overreach and a 29% drop in cases where the model does too little.

In Google’s testing, Carbon succeeded at cheating on Terminal Bench 4.0 zero times, with attempts falling to 0.4%. It also blocked every attack in a test of hidden prompt injections. These are Google’s own numbers, and outside testers will get their shot once the model is widely available.

How much will Gemini 4 Carbon cost?

Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input 95% cheaper. That matches Argon’s launch price. After the introductory period, 9to5Google reports the price will rise to $4 and $20.

Why is Google releasing Gemini 4 Carbon so fast?

Google says its researchers and models are working together to speed up progress. Not everyone is convinced the pace helps users. One 9to5Google reader questioned launching a new frontier model when most people still can’t fully use Argon.

Wall Street liked the news. Alphabet’s class A shares rose about 1.1% this afternoon.

For now, Google’s most capable model sits with the people paid to stop hackers. Everyone else waits.

data.title: Why YouTube keeps buffering for thousands of users today
data.description:
More than 24,000 YouTube users reported problems with the platform this morning, outage tracking data showed, as buffering, crashing and sign in errors spread across the United States starting around 10 20 a.m. Eastern time.


What YouTube users are actually experiencing

The outage began hitting users just as many were settling into their usual morning routine of checking videos, news clips and playlists. Reports started climbing quickly once the issue took hold, pointing to a widespread disruption rather than a handful of isolated complaints.


Outage tracking data shows a clear breakdown of what YouTube users are running into right now. Roughly 41% of reports point to buffering, where videos stall repeatedly instead of playing smoothly. Another 22% describe playback issues entirely, with videos failing to start at all. Crashing accounts for 19% of complaints, while sign in problems make up 11% and video quality issues round out the remaining 6%.

That spread of symptoms suggests the problem is not limited to a single feature. Instead, it appears to be touching multiple parts of how YouTube delivers video to users, from the initial loading process through to actual playback once a video begins streaming.

Why this outage is affecting so many people

Users across multiple cities have reported similar issues within minutes of each other, a pattern that typically points to a server side problem rather than something tied to an individual device, internet provider or region. When outages cluster this tightly in time, it almost always signals that YouTube’s own infrastructure, rather than something on the user end, is behind the disruption.

YouTube has dealt with outages of this kind before, including incidents in 2025 and earlier this year that affected hundreds of thousands of users at a time. Those previous outages were traced to issues ranging from server misconfigurations to problems with the recommendation system that powers the platform’s homepage.

As of this report, no official statement has confirmed the exact cause behind today’s disruption. Past outages have sometimes taken YouTube’s team close to an hour to fully resolve, while others cleared up within 20 to 30 minutes once engineers identified the source of the problem.

The timing of this outage is also significant, as it comes during a period of heavy daytime traffic when schools, offices and households are streaming content simultaneously. That kind of concentrated usage can sometimes amplify the visible impact of a server side issue, since more people are actively trying to load content the moment something goes wrong. Live streams and premieres scheduled for later today could also face delays or rescheduling if the underlying issue is not resolved quickly, since creators often depend on stable uploading and streaming tools to keep scheduled content on track.

How to tell if it is just you or a wider problem

For anyone currently dealing with buffering or crashing, there are a few quick ways to figure out whether the issue is widespread or specific to a single device. Checking an independent outage tracker can confirm whether reports are spiking broadly, rather than just on one phone, tablet or browser.

Restarting the YouTube app or refreshing the browser tab sometimes resolves temporary glitches, though during a confirmed platform wide outage, these steps typically will not fix anything until YouTube resolves the problem on its end. Switching between WiFi and mobile data can also help rule out a local internet issue versus a problem with YouTube itself.

Users who rely on YouTube TV for live programming may notice a separate but related set of issues, since that service runs on much of the same underlying infrastructure as the main YouTube platform. When one experiences disruption, the other sometimes follows shortly after.

Creators who depend on YouTube for daily income have historically voiced the loudest frustration during outages like this one, since even a short disruption can affect view counts, ad revenue and upload scheduling for channels that publish on a tight daily routine.

For now, the safest approach is to wait for an official update rather than repeatedly reinstalling the app or changing account settings, since those steps are unlikely to resolve a problem rooted in YouTube’s own servers. Keeping an eye on outage trackers remains the quickest way to know when service has returned to normal.

data.title: GTA 6 comes as a code in a box, and that’s the problem
data.description:
Physical copies of GTA 6 contain no disc. Instead, the box holds a code that buyers redeem on a PlayStation or Xbox store to download the game. Reports say the physical Standard Edition costs $79.99 and begins shipping Nov. 12, 2026, while the digital-only Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. The format has sparked a debate over ownership, game preservation and the future of physical games.


What is inside the box

According to reports, the physical edition is only available for the Standard Edition. Once a buyer redeems the code, the game is tied to that PlayStation or Xbox account. Reports also say that some physical copies have sold out at major retailers, which suggests that demand is strong even with the limits.


Why ownership is the sticking point

For many players, the core concern is that a physical purchase no longer carries the usual benefits. Disc games can be resold or traded, and they can be played without an online account. A redeemed code cannot be transferred the same way.

GTA 6 ‘An Extended Look’ officially premiered exactly 2 months ago today.

You just had to be there. https://t.co/satAfyaTfv

— GTA 6 Updates (@gtasix_) October 27, 2026

Critics also point to account risk. If a PlayStation or Xbox account is banned, a player could lose access to every digital game on it, including GTA 6. Some retailers have reportedly said they will not stock the game because it does not let buyers truly own what they pay for.

The demand behind the debate

Market data from a mobile research firm estimates that GTA 6 has sold 6.45 million digital pre-orders, generating about $630 million in revenue. A workforce software company reported that time-off requests for the game’s release date rose between 9% and 17%. The numbers show how large the audience is, and why even a code-in-a-box edition attracts buyers.

The hardware question

Some players are also questioning the cost of the hardware needed to play. Secondary-market prices for the PS5 Pro have reportedly reached $1,300 to $1,400, well above the manufacturer’s recommended retail price. One report claims the game may launch with a locked 30 frames per second and no full performance mode on PS5 Pro. That claim is not confirmed, and the publisher has not said whether it is accurate.

What comes next

The debate may reach beyond one game. One report says Sony plans to end disc production starting in 2028. If that happens, GTA 6’s no-disc approach could become a preview of how more publishers handle physical releases. For now, buyers have to decide whether a box with a code is worth the price.

data.title: Apple’s new iPad mini gets its biggest makeover ever
data.description:
Apple’s smallest tablet just got its biggest glow-up yet.


The tech giant unveiled an all-new iPad mini on Monday, Oct. 26, calling it the most significant update in the device’s history. The redesigned tablet features a larger OLED display, a thinner and lighter build, a powerful new A20 Pro chip and, for the first time, protection against water and dust.


Apple says the iPad mini has long been a favorite among a wide range of users, including creators, small business owners, doctors, field service workers and gamers, who appreciate having the full iPad experience in a device that fits in one hand.

A thinner design that can handle a splash

At just 5.4 millimeters thin, the new iPad mini is noticeably slimmer and lighter than the previous generation. It comes in two finishes, a new midnight shade and starlight.

The tablet also carries an IP67 rating, meaning it was tested to withstand dust and submersion in up to 1 meter of water for as long as 30 minutes. Apple notes that the protection could make the tablet a better fit for reading by the pool or working outside on a rainy day, though water resistance can decrease over time with normal wear.

A bigger, brighter screen

The headline feature is the new 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display. Thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner, Apple managed to make the screen bigger without changing the overall size of the device.

OLED technology allows for deeper blacks and richer color. The display reaches a peak brightness of 1,200 nits, which is more than twice as bright as the previous model, and it can dim down to just 1 nit for reading in bed at night. Shoppers can also choose a nano-texture option, previously offered on the iPad Pro, which cuts down on glare in bright settings.

A major boost in power

The A20 Pro chip, built on Apple’s latest 2-nanometer technology, gives the iPad mini a big jump in speed. Apple says the tablet delivers up to 4.5 times faster AI performance and up to 2.7 times faster graphics than the previous version, along with up to 60% faster multitasking performance for everyday jobs like editing photos.

The 512GB model also includes a more advanced Neural Engine with double the processing power of its predecessor, designed for heavier on-device AI work.

Better sound, cameras and connectivity

A new feature Apple calls Acoustic Display routes sound through the screen to deliver punchier bass and clearer highs. The 12MP front camera now sits on the long edge of the tablet, making video calls feel more natural in landscape mode, while the 12MP rear camera records 4K video and gains a new flash for sharper photos and document scans.

The tablet also features Apple’s own N1 wireless chip, which supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Cellular models include the C2 modem, which Apple says offers up to 50% faster data speeds.

Siri gets smarter

The iPad mini runs iPadOS 27, which includes Siri AI, an all-new version of the voice assistant now rolling out in beta. Siri AI can search across a user’s messages, emails and photos, respond to what’s on screen and answer questions on a wide range of topics. Apple notes that Siri AI is not available in the European Union or for users under 13, and some features come with daily usage limits.

Price and release date

Preorders open on Wednesday, Oct. 28, with the tablet arriving in stores on Friday, Nov. 6. The Wi-Fi model starts at $699, while the Wi-Fi and cellular version starts at $849. A new Smart Folio cover sells for $79.

This story was originally reported by Apple Newsroom.

data.title: Samsung News shutdown. Is your Galaxy phone affected?
data.description:
ow right now is to open Samsung News and look for the banner. If you see it, your device is included. If you do not, that does not mean you are safe. Samsung has a history of rolling out notices in waves, and tech outlet SamMobile, which first reported the notice, believes a worldwide shutdown is likely.


Many Galaxy owners may not notice at all. Plenty of longtime Samsung users have said online that they never knew the app existed, which may be part of the reason it is going away.


What happens to your Samsung News data?

Samsung says personal information, profiles and personalization settings connected to Samsung News will be deleted without undue delay once the service ends. The only exception is where local laws require the company to keep certain data for a set period, after which it will also be removed.

That deletion covers Samsung News only. Your Samsung account, Google account and everything else on your phone are not affected.

There is no export tool. If you follow specific publications, sports teams or stock trackers in the app, take screenshots of those settings before Dec. 21 so you can rebuild them somewhere else.

Why is Samsung shutting down Samsung News?

Samsung has not explained the decision, and this is where the timing gets interesting. In May, Samsung’s U.S. newsroom announced upgrades to Samsung News, including more video focused features and expanded content from premium publishers. Five months later, the app is on its way out.

It also marks the end of a short run. When Samsung shut down Samsung Free in December 2025, it told users to move to Samsung News. Barely a year later, that replacement is leaving too.

Samsung News is the fourth feed to occupy that leftmost Home screen slot since 2017. Bixby Home came first, then Samsung Daily in 2019, Samsung Free with One UI 3.0 in late 2020 and Samsung News in 2023. Each one was eventually replaced.

Is Samsung cutting other apps and features?

Yes, and the pattern is hard to miss. Samsung has been phasing out its Samsung Messages app in favor of Google Messages this year. It also plans to pull its AR Doodle and Quick Measure apps from the Galaxy Store on Dec. 31, 2026.

On the TV side, Microsoft will remove its Copilot AI assistant from Samsung and LG televisions on Dec. 1, 2026. That decision came from Microsoft, not Samsung, and Microsoft did not give a reason either. Copilot will remain available on web, desktop and mobile.

Taken together, Samsung appears to be trimming its own software and leaning harder on Google services and Galaxy AI, which expanded across the Home screen and Bixby with One UI 9.

What can replace Samsung News on a Galaxy phone?

Google Discover is the most obvious fallback. It already shares that leftmost panel on many Galaxy devices, and you can check your Home screen settings to turn it on. Samsung has not confirmed whether Discover will become the default or whether something new will take that spot.

Discover works differently, though. It recommends stories based on your Google activity, so it will not recreate the specific publications, scores and stock trackers you followed. If you want more control, a dedicated news app or an RSS reader is the better option.

What should Galaxy owners do now?

Open Samsung News and check for the notice. Screenshot anything you want to keep, set up Google Discover or another news app as a backup, then remove the widget whenever it suits you. The clock runs out on Dec. 21, and after that, Samsung’s newsfeed experiment closes its fourth chapter.

data.title: iOS 27.3 beta expected Monday with this 3 key new details
data.description:
Apple has barely finished rolling out iOS 27.2, and the next iPhone update is already on the horizon. iOS 27.3 is expected to reach testers within days, with a public release likely before the holidays.


iOS 27.2 arrived this week with new features for Messages, Siri AI and Photos, along with a refreshed Apple Music icon. Apple has not officially announced anything about iOS 27.3, so the details below are based on reports and past release patterns.


The release timeline

The first iOS 27.3 beta is expected as soon as Monday, Nov. 2. The public version should follow in mid-December, based on how Apple handled similar updates in past years.

  1. iOS 26.2 arrived Friday, Dec. 12.
  2. iOS 18.2 arrived Wednesday, Dec. 11.
  3. iOS 17.2 arrived Monday, Dec. 11.

Apple typically ships its last major software update of the year with some breathing room before the holiday break. That gives engineers time to build and release a quick fix if a serious problem turns up.

One quirk explains the numbering. Apple made iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo, which shifted every release in this cycle up by one number. The timing still follows the usual calendar.

The 2 features expected

Details will become clearer once the beta arrives, but two additions look likely.

  1. More Siri AI languages. Apple announced plans this week to expand language support, and iOS 27.3 could be where those changes reach users.
  2. A redesigned Health app. Reports say Apple has been reworking the app for some time to make health information easier to find and manage.

Security updates and bug fixes are also likely.

Which iPhones should get it

Based on current expectations, the update should be available for a wide range of models, from the iPhone 11 series through the iPhone 17 lineup and the iPhone 18 Pro models. The iPhone Air, iPhone Duo and both the second and third generation iPhone SE are also expected to be supported, along with the iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e.

Anyone who prefers to test early can watch for the beta next week. Those who would rather wait can expect the stable release closer to mid-December.

data.title: Capcom breach could turn into a phishing nightmare
data.description:
Capcom says no credit card data was taken. For the 11.7 million players caught in its latest breach, the bigger danger may land in their inboxes.


The Japanese video game company confirmed that hackers broke into Capcom ID, the single account system used across its online store and games, including Street Fighter 6 and the Resident Evil and Monster Hunter franchises. In total, 11,774,247 accounts worldwide were affected.


What the hackers took from Capcom ID

For nearly every affected account, the attackers accessed email addresses along with account details. Those details include the date each account was created, the time of the most recent login, how many times the user had logged in and the IP address used for that last session.

A smaller group of 43 accounts also had dates of birth, genders, countries or regions and nicknames exposed. The company said all other passwords were untouched and that no credit card information was involved. Games and online services are running normally.

Why the 196 accounts matter

The most revealing detail is the smallest number. The attackers changed the passwords on 196 accounts, apparently trying to lock their owners out. Capcom has since reset those credentials, and the affected players can log in again.

Capcom is forcing Ultimate Frame Data to take down its Street Fighter 6 section.

Capcom’s legal team says the site contains hitbox and collision data that isn’t normally accessible through regular gameplay, and that Capcom doesn’t authorize the use of modified software or analysis tools to obtain game data.

The site was asked to remove or disable access to the SF6 data by October 30. The owner, MetalMusicMan, has already taken the section offline, saying: “Not my choice, sorry everyone.”

— Pirat_Nation 🔴 (@Pirat_Nation) October 23, 2026

That shows the intruders were not just copying data. They took control of real accounts, at least briefly.

The stolen details create a second risk. An email address paired with someone’s real login history is valuable for phishing. A scammer who knows when a player last signed in and how often they play can write a fake Capcom message that looks convincing.

Capcom is warning users to be cautious of unexpected emails and messages that ask for personal information or include links and attachments. The company plans to notify affected customers in stages and has set up regional support contacts.

A timeline Capcom moved on quickly

The company detected suspicious activity and confirmed unauthorized access on Monday, Oct. 19. By the next day, it was clear that customer data had been compromised. A day after that, the company reported the incident to police and to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission.

The company says it has identified how the attackers got in and added safeguards to stop a repeat. It has not said when the intrusion began or who was behind it, and no group has claimed responsibility, according to sources.

Capcom has been here before</st

Okay, hear me out…🚀

Either Capcom or Bloober Team should buy Dead Space IP, and make more remakes and new games.

They are the perfect candidates, since EA’s mediocre a** doesn’t wanna make games like these and focus on their god-awful shooters and sports games.

What do you think?😎

— Rino🚀 (@RinoTheBouncer) October 23, 2026

rong>

This is not the company’s first major attack. In November 2020, the ransomware group Ragnar Locker claimed to have stolen 1 terabyte of Capcom data in an incident that may have affected up to 390,000 people. Capcom later disclosed that the attackers had entered through an outdated VPN device.

The timing of the new breach is awkward. It comes as the new Street Fighter movie plays in theaters worldwide, putting one of Capcom’s oldest franchises in the spotlight. For most players, the fallout will come later, in messages that look like Capcom but are not.

data.title: Can a wrong update date hurt your Android phone’s security?
data.description:
Why are so many Android phones suddenly claiming to run a Google Play System update from January 1, 2027, and should owners be worried? The short answer is no. The odd date appears to be a labeling mistake rather than a sign of anything wrong with the phones themselves.


The glitch has been spotted on the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Google Pixel 8 Pro and Vivo X300 Ultra, along with other Android devices. Reports on Reddit indicate it is also affecting phones running Android 12, including older models. Samsung users with the stable One UI 9.0 software reportedly received a roughly 100 MB update before noticing the date.


What is behind the strange date

Google Play System updates let Google refresh certain Android components, such as services, security elements and compatibility features, without a full operating system upgrade. The date appearing now is not a sign that Google has released a future version of Android. According to reports, it is most likely a metadata or labeling error inside the update itself. Google has not published a detailed changelog and has not explained the cause.

Does it affect performance or security

So far, there is no evidence that the incorrect date changes how phones run, how apps work or how well devices perform. It also does not mean a phone has received security patches from January 2027. The Google Play System update date is separate from both the Android version and the security patch level, so owners who want to confirm their phone is up to date should check each of those details on its own.

The real downside is confusion. With the wrong date showing, it becomes harder to tell which Google Play System update is actually installed.

How to check your update

Open Settings, then go to Security and Privacy or About Phone, depending on the device. Tap Google Play System update, review the date shown and install any update that is offered. On Samsung phones, the option is usually found under Settings, Security and privacy, Updates, then Google Play system update, though the menu path can differ by software version.

Should you reset your phone

No. Reports suggest that changing the date and time settings or resetting the phone does not correct the displayed timestamp, so a factory reset is unnecessary. Google has not said when a fix will arrive, so users can leave their phones as they are and watch for a correction in a future update.

data.title: Switch 2 cracked open: Is Mario Kart World now moddable?
data.description:
Can an AI coding agent crack one of the most locked-down game consoles on the market? A security researcher says yes. Their jailbreak of the Nintendo Switch 2 is now public, and it has Nintendo fans asking how long it will last.


The researcher, a student who posts online as pepsipu, shared a video of Mario Kart World running with extra characters added, including Peter Griffin, Hatsune Miku, Cinnamoroll and an Angry Bird. The clip suggests the exploit is real. The creator also published a detailed write-up of the process, which is a bold move given Nintendo’s aggressive legal history.


How the jailbreak was built

The project took about two weeks and relied heavily on OpenAI’s Codex coding agent. The researcher first built a test setup around both a Switch 1 and a Switch 2 so the AI could work with as little human help as possible. Remote devices sent controller inputs over USB and captured video over HDMI, while a Bluetooth switch pressed the power button whenever the console crashed and needed a restart.

i jailbroke the nintendo switch 2

so i modded cinnamoroll, peter griffin, hatsune miku, and more into Mario Kart World, a switch 2 exclusive

now watch my friends and i get cooked by bots

learn more and get the exploit https://t.co/ykjgyfrFRp https://t.co/BOcFhejRz1

— pepsipu (@pepsipu) October 22, 2026

Codex first tried the console’s browser, but that route went nowhere. It then turned to SmileBASIC 4, a $25 game-building app sold in Nintendo’s eShop. There, the AI found an integer overflow, a type of software bug, that gave it a foothold in the console’s file system services. The Mario Kart World mods came together in about a day.

What the hack can and cannot do

The exploit is tethered, which means it disappears whenever the console shuts down and must be reapplied. It is also not a full kernel-level jailbreak. Even so, it should open the door to homebrew software, game modding and deeper reverse engineering. It works on firmware version 23.0.1.

Will Nintendo respond?

Probably, and quickly. Nintendo could remove SmileBASIC 4 from its store, push out a firmware update that closes the hole, or do both. The jailbreak also arrives right after a PlayStation 5 jailbreak surfaced, which can run PS2 emulators with support for original discs.

Why it matters

The bigger story may be the method. A small team, or even one person, used an AI agent to physically operate hardware, test ideas and find a flaw in a heavily protected system. Console makers now have to assume that tools like this will speed up the hunt for weaknesses.
